subject: literature
passage: Kofi had expected his aunt's bicycle shop to be quiet on a Saturday morning. Instead, customers were already waiting at the door when she unlocked it. One needed a new chain; another wanted a flat tire fixed. His aunt handed him a wrench and a tin of grease without a word. By noon his hands were black, his shirt was ruined, and he had repaired his first tire by himself.
stem: According to the text, how was the morning at the shop different from what Kofi had expected?

choices.A: His aunt asked him to open the shop by himself.
choices.B: Customers were already waiting when the shop opened.
choices.C: His aunt would not let him work on any bicycles.
choices.D: The shop had run out of new chains and tires.

explanation.why: The first sentence tells us what Kofi expected: a quiet Saturday morning. The next sentence begins with "Instead," which signals the difference: "customers were already waiting at the door when she unlocked it."
explanation.A: Incorrect. The text says his aunt unlocked the shop; it never says Kofi opened it alone.
explanation.B: Correct. This restates the sentence that begins with "Instead": the shop was busy, not quiet, from the moment it opened.
explanation.C: Incorrect. His aunt handed him tools, and he repaired a tire, so she clearly let him work.
explanation.D: Incorrect. A customer needed a new chain, but the text never says the shop had none.
